title: Olfactory Coding in Ventral CA1 Region of the Hippocampus
text:
This research will contribute fundamental insights into what role ventral hippocampus, a part of the brain
involved in memory and emotion, plays in sense of smell. In the short term, this research will provide
knowledge about the structure of neural connections that may carry odor information from the primary olfactory
cortex directly to ventral hippocampus, and it will define the responses of single-cells and groups of cells in
ventral hippocampus to odors. In the long term, these investigations will inform scientific studies into why
sense of smell is affected in neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Dynamic Free-Breathing 129Xe MRI for Functional Lung Imaging in Children
text:
Chronic respiratory diseases significantly impact pediatric populations, yet current tools for assessing lung
function, like spirometry and CT, have limitations, particularly in young children. This proposal seeks to
establish free breathing 129Xe MRI as a safe, non-invasive imaging tool that provides high-sensitivity functional
information across pediatric age groups. By optimizing this technique, demonstrating its clinical utility in early
childhood, and extending its feasibility to neonates and infants, this work aims to transform pediatric lung
imaging, enabling earlier diagnosis, better disease monitoring, and improved clinical outcomes.

title: Facility Core
text: SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: FACILITY CORE The Facility Core (FC) for the Great Lakes Center for Fresh Waters and Human Health, hosted by the University of Michigan (UM), will provide support services for four individual projects and the Community Engagement Core. The FC is divided into three subcores: nutrient analysis, led by the Stone Laboratory, Ohio State University; cyanotoxin analysis, provided by SUNY-College of Environmental Science and Forestry (ESF), University of Toledo (UT), and Wayne State University (WSU); and DNA sequencing and data synthesis at UM. Each of the participating universities has extensive experience in their respective areas of analytical expertise. All cores from the prior award period remain as members of the proposed renewal Center, which will ensure continuity in data integrity. New to this application, we have greatly expanded the mass spectrometry analysis portion of the core to include both new facilities available at SUNY-ESF and extensive new capabilities available at WSU and UT. DNA sequencing has been moved from a private company via the Administrative Core to a UM core via the FC in this renewal to better integrate data across the different projects.

title: Identifying mis-splicing-derived antigens in spliceosomal mutant myelodysplasia and targeting via T-cell receptor therapeutics
text:
Splicing factor gene mutations are prevalent in blood disorders and induce widespread, recurrent alternative
splicing events. We propose a novel approach of targeting these mutations via antigen-based
immunotherapies, based on the hypothesis that mis-spliced mRNAs give rise to meaningful tumor antigens.
The proposed research will (1) contribute to the understanding of mis-spliced mRNAs as immunotherapeutic
targets and (2) inspire T-cell receptor therapies for myelodysplastic syndromes and immunoprevention
strategies for clonal hematopoiesis with spliceosomal mutations.

title: MR Metabolic Imaging of Multiple Sclerosis
text:
The proposed research will expand and further validate the use of new metabolic imaging in Multiple Sclerosis
(MS). New techniques for non-invasive assessment of neuroinflammatory and redox processes will be
investigated in MS models, while metabolic imaging will be applied to monitor therapy response in people living
with MS. Results from this proposal will serve to ameliorate clinical management of MS patients, help refine
therapeutic regimens and, ultimately, lead to better outcome and patient quality of life.

title: Circadian control of neuroinflammation after spinal cord injury
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because spinal cord injury causes permanent disability and
worsened quality of life. Targeting harmful neuroinflammation after spinal cord injury could lead to discovery of
new therapies that improve tissue repair and functional recovery. This preclinical project aims to reveal the
untapped therapeutic potential of the circadian-neuroimmune axis after spinal cord injury, and is therefore
relevant to NIH’s mission to seek fundamental knowledge that improves health and reduces disability.

title: Designing probiotic strains to sense and deliver novel treatments for oral cancer
text:
Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a prevalent cancer with limited treatment options due to therapeutic
resistance and immune evasion within the tumor microenvironment (TIME). This project aims to develop an
innovative therapeutic strategy using engineered Lactobacillus fermentum to deliver immune-activating
components, specifically CCL5 or a novel CCL5-NBαPD1 fusion protein, to reprogram the OSCC TIME and
enhance antitumor immunity. By leveraging the natural properties of L. fermentum, this approach seeks to
overcome current limitations and improve patient outcomes in OSCC.

title: Dissecting the role of thalamic withdrawal-encoding ensembles in opioid use disorder
text:
The aversive state of opioid withdrawal is a major driver of relapse, yet the circuit-level mechanisms of this
process remain undefined. This project will define how the paraventricular thalamus (PVT) encodes spontaneous
and precipitated withdrawal and identify the circuit adaptations that contribute to heroin seeking. By elucidating
these mechanisms, this proposal will uncover circuit-level targets to disrupt the withdrawal-relapse cycle and
improve long-term outcomes in OUD.

title: TUFCCC/HC Regional Comprehensive Cancer Health Partnership
text: Populations in the PA-NJ-NYC region experience significant cancer-related health morbidity and mortality across the cancer continuum, from a higher prevalence of cancer risk factors to delayed screening and diagnoses, experiencing more advanced disease, and poorer outcomes. SPEECH has made significant strides toward transforming cancer health research and education; research infrastructure and platforms that enabled investigators to advance cancer health excellence in research, career development, and capacity-building. In the next five years, our Partnership aims to further advance cancer health research, training and, locally-informed interventions with innovative multidisciplinary projects conducted by basic, clinical and population science researchers and outstanding and promising trainees.

title: Assessing the Role of HIV-specific IgA glycosylation on transport and function
text:
Despite extensive research efforts, there is currently no vaccine for human immunodeficiency virus
(HIV). The failure of a recent clinical trial (AMP) using passively transferred broadly neutralizing anti-HIV
immunoglobulin G (IgG) monoclonal antibodies to confer protection highlights the need for alternative preventive
strategies. The proposed research aims to characterize and exploit the biochemical properties of newly
discovered broadly neutralizing anti-HIV IgA, with the goal of informing the design of future vaccine candidates
and immunotherapeutic approaches.

title: Quantitative 3D imaging of cerebral blood flow during stroke
text:
Imaging and quantification of cerebral blood flow is crucial for understanding stroke progression
and developing new treatments. Current methods for measuring blood flow in preclinical stroke
models lack the ability to quantitatively compare blood flow across subjects and over long
periods. In this project we will develop two new advances in laser speckle imaging that will
improve the quantitative accuracy and repeatability of blood flow images and allow depth-
resolved blood flow imaging for the first time.

title: Contribution of the sacral neural crest to the peripheral nervous system of the post-umbilical gastrointestinal tract
text:
The enteric nervous system (ENS) is a critical part of the peripheral nervous system that controls gut
motility and other functions. Abnormal development of ENS leads to life threatening disorders like Hirschsprung’s
disease. Our results will provide important clues regarding mistakes that may lead to birth defects in the ENS.

title: Core 2: Biostatistics Shared Resource Core
text: The purpose of the Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Shared Resource Core (BBSRC) is to provide professional expertise in biostatistics and bioinformatics for all Meharry Medical College/Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center/Tennessee State University Cancer Partnership (MVTCP) projects, investigators and participants. Functions provided by this core include development of experimental designs and power and sample size analysis; data quality control; statistical and bioinformatic analysis and interpretation of findings; and collaboration on presentation of results. To achieve these functions, BBSRC directors and members are constantly available to investigators and are in regular contact with project and Core leaders.

title: Improving the prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia by identifying kidney-based risk factors
text:
In the US 50,000 infants each year are born less than 28 weeks of gestation, and severe bronchopulmonary
dysplasia (BPD) poses a tremendous health and economic burden in these infants. This foundational work
seeks to improve severe BPD prediction by a) focusing on kidney-based risk factors of acute kidney injury and
fluid overload and b) identifying critical biomarker candidates. Improving severe BPD predication with kidney-
based risk factors and biomarkers will facilitate individualized fluid management and improved AKI detection
and treatment, decreasing the diagnosis and severity of BPD in prematurely born infants.

title: Investigation of Key Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Metabolism Pathway Roles in Support of Epstein-Barr Virus Replication
text:
(3 sentences)
As an orally transmitted pathogen, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) crosses the tonsillar epithelium and
infects B cells, whereupon reaching the memory B-cell compartment it establishes lifelong
infection. In this proposal, we will investigate how EBV subverts cellular cell nicotinamide
adenine dinucleotide metabolism pathways to support efficient viral lytic replication, including in
nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. This research promises to lay a foundation for novel host
metabolism targeted therapeutic approaches to block EBV lytic gene expression.

title: Mechanisms in Membrane Dynamics
text:
A defining feature of cells are membrane bilayers that separate them from their environment and, in human and
other eukaryotic cells, delineate intracellular compartments with specialized functions. Here we address the
fundamental question how cells make and maintain these membranes. Dysfunction in membrane lipid
homeostasis is linked to a number of neurological disorders, including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases,
among many others. Our work will inform regarding disease mechanism, prerequisite for the development of
therapeutic strategies.

title: Transcriptional Mechanisms of Drug Addiction
text:
Addiction remains one of the world’s greatest public health problems, yet its pathophysiology remains
incompletely understood and available treatments for addictions to various drugs of abuse are inadequately
effective for most people. This Program Project Grant focuses on mechanisms of transcriptional and chromatin
regulation in drug action on a cell-type-specific basis in brain reward regions. Our work is contributing to a
better understanding of the neurobiological basis of stimulant and opioid addiction, which we believe is
necessary for the eventual development of definitive treatments and cures for these substance use disorders.

title: Engineer Biomimetic Microfluidic Models to Investigate and Reprogram Tumor Associated Neutrophils for Cancer Therapy
text:
Neutrophils provide a critical defense against infection, but they can also promote tumor progression and
metastasis in the aggressive glioblastoma. This study will employ a novel strategy to interrogate neutrophil
biology and reprogram tumor-associated neutrophils into antitumor effector cells, which will have implications for
developing novel neutrophil-targeted strategies for treating cancer, neutropenia and inflammation.

title: Improving the prediction of opioid outcomes via automated EHR data processing
text:
Severe opioid adverse drug effects (ADEs), including persistent use, tolerance, and opioid use disorder (OUD)
remain significant public health challenges, yet risk identification is often hindered by inconsistencies in electronic
health record (EHR) data and human data processing limitations. This project aims to overcome these issues by
developing an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework that leverages automated machine learning,
knowledge graphs, and large language models to improve and standardize EHR data quality. Through human-
AI collaboration, this approach will optimize data cleaning, streamline feature engineering, and uncover novel
ADE risk factors, ultimately improving clinical decision-making and facilitating personalized risk assessments.

title: Multinuclear MRI to Assess Joint Homeostasis after Knee Injury
text:
Post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) is a common occurrence after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture in-
dependently of patient treatment, which indicates that early cellular and molecular changes directly after injury
seem to be critical in disease development. The goal of this study is to develop a predictive model of progression
to PTOA using a combination of multinuclear magnetic resonance imaging markers, soluble synovial ﬂuid biolog-
ical markers, and biomechanical markers acquired on patients just after ACL injury, and at different time points
after joint repair. This prognostic combination of biomarkers will help identify therapeutic targets and monitor the
efﬁcacy of intervention in the development of preventive treatments of PTOA.
